prompt: Was the founder of the bank that was established 42 years before the National Banking Act was expanded to include the Territory of Hawai'i still alive when it acquired Pioneer Federal Savings Bank?
answer: No. The bank was First Hawaiian Bank, founded in 1858 as Bishop & Co. by Charles Reed Bishop—42 years before the 1900 extension of national-banking legislation to Hawaiʻi. Bishop died in 1915, whereas First Hawaiian acquired Pioneer Federal Savings Bank decades later, so he was not alive at the time of the acquisition.
